proposals.source_excerpt: [F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] and [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]: the noise coordinates are independent standard normals with even density, first and third moments zero, and second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$.
proposals.proposed_replacement: [F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] supplies independent standard-normal coordinates with normalized density $\varphi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$ and covariance one. We use the scalar calculation of [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]] with this supplied law, rather than invoke its AC-based law construction: $\varphi\prime(t)=-t\varphi(t)$, so integration by parts on $[-R,R]$ gives $\int t^2\varphi=[-t\varphi]_{-R}^R+\int\varphi$ and $\int t^4\varphi=[-t^3\varphi]_{-R}^R+3\int t^2\varphi$. The polynomial-Gaussian boundary terms vanish as $R\to\infty$; the nonnegative integrals increase to their full integrals. Supplied normalization therefore gives second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$; symmetry gives first and third moments zero. This supplied-law calculation uses no additional choice.

cases.original_concern: The Statement defines a positive Hopf band solely as 'an oriented annulus whose two boundary components, with their induced orientations, have linking number +1.' This omits the unknotted-core condition. A framed annulus around a nontrivial knot can satisfy this linking condition. Knotting the b-annulus away from the plumbing square and the specified disk for a⁺ preserves the stated linking/intersection conditions and matrix calculation, but does not justify the trefoil boundary identification in Proof 1.1. The later word 'standard' needs an explicit restriction consistent with the initial definition. The conventional missing condition is explicit in Quach Hongler–Weber, §2, printed p. 137: [The link of an extrovert divide](https://www.numdam.org/article/AFST_2000_6_9_1_133_0.pdf). Thus the definition and trefoil identification appear overbroad as written, although the displayed matrix follows from the other specified conditions.

cases.reason: Linking of the induced annulus boundaries fixes its framing, not its knot type. A tubular annulus with nontrivial core and this framing meets the written definition. Local knotting of the second annulus away from the plumbing square and the first push-off disk does not change the given framing/intersection/linking conditions. Proof1.1, in contrast, uses the actual standard disk-and-three-band model; that geometric identification does not follow for these more general annuli. Add the missing unknotted-core condition for the conventional trefoil assertion and retain the original matrix-only result for all annuli satisfying the original hypotheses, since Proof2.1 depends only on those data.

cases.original_concern: Fact F7 states 'Linking of disjoint oriented curves is the signed intersection with a spanning two-chain' and cites thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection. The fact strengthens the cited interface without explaining the chain extension. cases.reason: The signed-intersection supplier is explicitly conditional on a supplied embedded smooth spanning surface, transverse circle and diagram; it does not state the arbitrary singular-chain extension attributed in F7. Actual Proof2.1 needs only zero linking across separated balls. The existing Seifert-pairing definition defines linking as the meridian coefficient in complement homology. A cycle bounding an integral chain in its own ball is zero in the complement of the other ball, so its coefficient is zero. Replace the excessive Fact with that exact already-used homological argument; the surjection Statement and every category/choice premise stay unchanged.

proposals.source_excerpt: [F7] Linking of disjoint oriented curves is the signed intersection with a spanning two-chain. [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]
proposals.proposed_replacement: [F7] For disjoint oriented curves, linking is the positive-meridian coefficient of the first curve in the homology of the complement of the second, extended additively over integral one-cycles. A cycle in a ball disjoint from the second curve bounds an integral singular two-chain in that ball, since a ball is contractible. Its complement-homology class and hence its linking coefficient are zero. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]
